key_insight: Synthetic biomedical data is valuable for building and testing machine learning models, but performance on simulated data often overestimates real-world performance. The paper highlights the simulation-to-reality gap as the key barrier to turning virtual experiments into reliable biomedical insight.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of using synthetic datasets in biomedical ML when models perform well in simulation but fail to generalize to real patient data. It explains why synthetic success does not automatically translate into clinical usefulness.
method: Reviews how synthetic data are generated and used as a proxy for expensive or sensitive biomedical experiments.
Analyzes the simulation-to-reality gap between virtual benchmarks and real-world deployment conditions.
Discusses strategies for evaluating and improving the realism, robustness, and transferability of synthetic-data-driven models.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the paper provides a practical warning: synthetic data can accelerate development, but validation on real-world data remains essential. It helps teams design better experiments, choose stronger evaluation protocols, and avoid overtrusting synthetic performance.
visual_elements: A side-by-side pipeline showing synthetic training data versus real-world clinical deployment
A gap diagram illustrating the simulation-to-reality mismatch
A workflow chart for generating, validating, and transferring synthetic biomedical data
Icons for model training, patient data, and clinical validation
paper_title: From virtual experiments to biomedical insight with synthetic data
paper_authors: Margarida Victoriano, Milena Pavlović, Geir Kjetil Sandve, Hélder P. Oliveira, Artur Rocha
